values.value: What does the destination tenant look like today — is there an MCE instance, does it have a business-unit structure, and is it agreed which brand or region lands in which BU?

[{"value":1,"label":"No MCE tenant provisioned, or one exists that nobody administers. Business-unit structure is undecided."},{"value":2,"label":"A tenant and some business units exist, but which brand, region or source instance lands where has not been agreed."},{"value":3,"label":"Tenant and business units are live and administered, and every brand or region has an agreed destination BU."}]

docs/specs/tier-2/sfmc-target-adapter.md §7.1 — "Each SFMCTargetAdapter.generate() invocation is scoped to one (target SFMC instance, business unit) pair. The adapter does not iterate across instances or BUs", and §7 opening, "a representative engagement might span 5 source instances -> 3 target instances with several BUs each". The BU map is therefore not tenant trivia: it is the count of adapter runs and of parallel build tracks, which is why this one carries horizon_driver. Named target_bu_structure rather than business_unit_structure because the latter is already a scored ESTATE COMPLEXITY dimension asking the opposite question — how the SOURCE account is split — and rule 6 exists to stop a supplement quietly landing on a scored key. The same spec's out-of-scope list names "Business Unit setup / provisioning, IP warm-up, CRM connector config" as tenant config that is gap-doc'd, not generated — so if it does not exist, somebody has to build it before the accelerator has anywhere to write.
